_comment: Reference completion hashes for the three published Laguna decode arms, so
that a reproduction can be checked against OUR result and not merely
against itself. Without this file a reproducer can only prove
self-consistency: run twice, get the same answer, learn nothing about
whether it is the same answer we got.
Each sha is sha256(completion_text)[:16] -- the value decode_bench.py writes
to its --json-out. Produced at 256 max_tokens, temperature 0, gamma 6,
fp8 KV, 8192 max seq len, single stream. These are the fp8/8192 regime of
the published decode table, NOT the bf16/3072 interactive stack that
serve_prod.sh launches -- the two disagree and the hashes are not shared.
Verified across a cold clone and cold build against the original run:
Note that the arms deliberately do NOT all agree with each other. DFlash is
meant to be output-identical to serial, and is on 5 of 6 rows. The g_proj
GEMV arm differs from both on 4 rows by design: it removes a ~1 ulp BF16
error present in the baseline GEMM, so some argmax ties break the other way.
That is why this file is keyed per arm and the arms are not cross-checked.
Check a run with:  python3 bench/laguna/check_repro.py --arm <arm> <json>

nogproj.description: DFlash speculative decode at gamma=6, g_proj GEMV OFF.

prose.note: The one row that does not reproduce. On every DFlash arm this prompt suspends to serial decode by design (adaptive_spec drops it below ADAPTIVE_MIN, reported as adapt_suspend=1 at roughly the serial rate), and on this arm its text is not stable run to run. A mismatch here is a known open item, not evidence your build is wrong. The same prompt IS stable on the gproj arm. See README.

gproj.description: DFlash gamma=6 plus the g_proj verify GEMV. The shipping stack.
